candidates.tagline: The NSA's classified network went down during routine maintenance — the same routine it uses to monitor everyone else's
candidates.story: On November 17, 2026, the NSA's classified internal communications network, NSANet, went offline during what the agency described as 'scheduled routine maintenance'; a defense official confirmed the disruption but assured that 'mission-critical capabilities' were not affected — a classic understatement from the organization whose entire job is never going offline.
candidates.why_funny: The organization whose entire mission is to monitor, intercept, and secure global communications for the US intelligence community couldn't maintain its own classified communications network through basic scheduled maintenance.
candidates.alt: Aerial photograph of the NSA headquarters complex at Fort Meade, Maryland, showing the distinctive black glass main office buildings, parking structures, antenna arrays, and surrounding facilities of the National Security Agency campus

candidates.tagline: Amazon removed the Kindle's bezel, accidentally replaced it with a glowing ring of light bleed, then said it was 'expected'
candidates.story: Amazon's new 2026 Kindle eliminated the physical bezel for a sleek flush-glass design, but the edge lighting bleeds through the glass in dark mode, creating a bright glowing ring along all four edges; when users complained, Amazon's official response was that this was 'expected' to achieve a 'color bezel' — meaning Amazon's solution for the bezel-free design was to accidentally create a bezel made of light.
candidates.why_funny: Amazon's design goal was to remove the bezel; the design they shipped created one out of light bleed; and Amazon's official position is that a glowing fake bezel was always the plan.
candidates.alt: Amazon Kindle 2026 e-readers in four colors — black, gold, rose, and denim — displayed together, showing the new bezel-free flush-glass design that introduced the light bleed issue on the base model
